episodes.158443: A thunderstorm along an outflow boundary moved across the Treasure Coast International Airport  and produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.158444: A man on Melbourne Beach was struck by lightning as a thunderstorm moved from the mainland to the barrier island and offshore. The man was injured, but survived.
episodes.158569: Residual moisture from previous days convection helped to prime the atmosphere which led to an uptick in shower and thunderstorm coverage across western Colorado. Some storms produced heavy rain which led to localized debris flows across the Grizzly Creek Fire burn scar.
episodes.158753: A thunderstorm briefly became severe in the Four Corners area, producing wind gusts near 60 mph.
episodes.158756: A thunderstorm became severe over northern Butte County, producing wind gusts near 75 mph.
episodes.158758: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over the northeastern Black Hills, producing quarter sized hail south of Nemo.
episodes.158760: A severe thunderstorm developed over the southern Black Hills, producing hail to quarter size from south of Custer to near Pringle.
episodes.158762: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over eastern Jackson County, producing hail and wind gusts around 60 mph.
episodes.158763: A severe thunderstorm brought wind gusts over 60 mph in northeastern Jackson County.
episodes.158837: With an area of high pressure still over the Four Corners area and an abundant amount of moisture across New Mexico, it was another active day with widespread thunderstorms on July 3, 2021. Thunderstorms developed early in the day across the high terrain and then tracked in a south to southwest direction onto lower elevations. There was one report of a flash flood in the Magado Creek near Capitan. The Magado Creek rose an estimated ten feet which flooded low-lying areas and trapped two unoccupied vehicles. Fortunately, there were no injuries or fatalities.
episodes.159086: Severe thunderstorm moved across Goshen County on the second producing hailstones up to two inches in diameter. A trained spotter noted that the two inch hail blanketed the ground in addition to ripping paint off their home and destroying their garden plants.
episodes.159091: Severe thunderstorm moved across Cheyenne County producing hailstones up to one inch in diameter. Spotter noted that nearby crops were damaged and associated wind gusts from thunderstorm knocked down two power line poles.
episodes.159092: Severe thunderstorm over Goshen County and the community of Huntley produced hailstones up to one inch in diameter.
episodes.159110: A nearby station measured severe outflow winds from a collapsing storm.
episodes.159875: A cold pool aloft caused numerous showers and an isolated thunderstorm across eastern MA.
episodes.160020: Isolated thunderstorms produced large hail and a brief tornado across parts of northwest Nebraska, primarily Sheridan and Cherry Counties, the evening of July 3.
episodes.160207: A compact short-wave trough moved over central North Dakota resulting in thunderstorm development. Instability was elevated and deep layer shear was marginal. This was enough, though, for large hail to develop over parts of the James River Valley. The largest hail was the size of a ping pong ball, which occurred northeast of Napoleon in Logan County.
episodes.160752: A stalled front served as a focus for widespread showers and thunderstorms. Heavy rainfall resulted in flooding across parts of the area.
episodes.160859: A severe thunderstorms produced large hail in central Adams County.  The hail ranged from quarter to golf ball size.
episodes.160861: Severe thunderstorms produced damaging winds, large hail, and two weak landspouts over Logan, Morgan and Washington counties.  Large hail, up to ping pong ball size and wind gusts to 60 mph, caused minor tree damage.
episodes.160881: Severe storms developed along a warm front over central and north central South Dakota. The slow moving thunderstorms produced hail for a half-hour in Jones and Dewey counties. Wind gusts of 70 mph in Jones County caused damage to corn crops.
episodes.160900: A cold front was across the Permian Basin. The upper level winds were fairly weak, and there was a lot of moisture in the atmosphere. Outflow boundaries from thunderstorms were present across the area. There was enhanced lift and convergence along the front and outflow boundaries. These conditions resulted in thunderstorms that produced hail and damaging winds across portions of West Texas. Flash flooding also occurred due to heavy rain that moved over saturated soils.
episodes.160959: Strong thunderstorms developed in the afternoon over the high terrain of central and southern Arizona before spreading to the lower deserts through the evening, with new development driven mostly by strong outflow boundaries. The primary outflow boundary moved southwest with widespread 30-40 mph wind gusts observed across south-central Arizona and a few stronger gusts, including a 59 mph gust in southern Gila county. The winds were strong enough to cause hundreds of power outages in the Phoenix metro area and generate dense blowing dust over the open deserts in Pinal and western Maricopa counties. With above normal moisture levels, storms also produced localized flash flooding mostly in foothill/high terrain areas, including flash flooding enhanced by recent burn scars.
episodes.161015: Thunderstorms developed across southeast Arizona in the afternoon, with strong cells pulsing up over terrain features and outflow boundaries. With precipitable water values near record levels for early-July and very slow steering flow, storms were capable of producing very heavy rain over the same areas, with rain rates around 1-2 inches per hour, resulting in localized flash flooding. Heavy rain from strong storms that developed over Pinal Peak experienced enhanced runoff due to the recent Telegraph burn scar. Runoff from these storms collected in the many dry washes with flow over forest service roads.
episodes.161253: A shortwave moved through Central New York, triggering scattered thunderstorms. Several storms produced torrential rainfall which led to flash flooding. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain fell over the southern part of Broome county in approximately a 3 to 4 hour time span.
episodes.161254: A shortwave moved through Northeast Pennsylvania, triggering scattered thunderstorms. Several storms produced torrential rainfall which led to areas of flash flooding. A narrow band of rainfall totaling 2 to 4 inches stretched across the northeast quarter of the county. This rain fell in under 4 hours.
episodes.161353: In the afternoon and evening hours on July 2nd, a stalled frontal boundary draped across northern Louisiana, central Mississippi and Alabama. This left moist, unstable air across southern Louisiana and much drier continental air to the north. This boundary, along with a upper-level weak disturbance helped ignite slow-moving scattered showers and thunderstorms that led to flash flooding.
episodes.161354: In the afternoon and evening hours on July 2nd, a stalled frontal boundary draped across northern Louisiana, central Mississippi and Alabama bordered moist, unstable air across Louisiana to the south from much drier continental air to the north. This boundary, along with a upper-level weak disturbance helped ignite a few strong to severe thunderstorms across marine areas across Lake Pontchartrain.
episodes.161376: Hurricane Elsa passed about 200 miles to the south of the southern coast of PR. However, outer rainbands associated with the tropical cyclone affected the southern half of Puerto Rico with periods of heavy rains and gusty winds.
episodes.161443: A slow moving thunderstorm produced flooding in Orange County.
episodes.161477: Scattered thunderstorms moved west across southeast Arizona. Storms produced flash flooding and a swath of damaging winds across the Tucson Metro area, and a landspout was also observed. A swift water rescue with two injuries occurred in Cornfield Canyon in western Cochise County.
episodes.161519: Scattered thunderstorms moved developed and moved west across southeast Arizona. Storms produced heavy rain from late morning into early afternoon causing flash flooding in parts of Santa Cruz, western Cochise, and southeast Pima counties.
episodes.161569: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms occurred through mid evening across the mountains, mountain valleys, and locations along and west of I-25. The severe threat was low, though a stronger storm or two did occur. An isolated flash flooding threat was also noted on this day, and did occur with the Spring Burn Scar observing heavy rainfall and flash flooding.
episodes.161570: Isolated showers and storms occurred along the I-25 corridor during the afternoon on this day, especially around and north of Pueblo. There was additional development across the eastern plains, but both areas really only observed isolated severe storms.
episodes.161635: High pressure centered near the Four Corners brought moisture over Arizona which developed into strong thunderstorms.
episodes.161698: Low pressure meandering along a stalled frontal boundary produced scattered showers and thunderstorms across the region. With light upper level flow, these storms were generally slow moving, resulting in flash flooding across parts of New York City and the Lower Hudson Valley. Rainfall amounts in the heaviest storms ranged from around 1 to 1.5 inches.
episodes.161700: Low pressure meandering along a stalled frontal boundary produced scattered showers and thunderstorms across the region. With light upper level flow, these storms were generally slow moving, resulting in flash flooding across portions of urban northeast New Jersey. Rainfall amounts in the heaviest storms ranged from around 1 to 1.5 inches, including 1.47 inches reported by the Newark Airport ASOS.

events.narrative: Debris and mudflow were noted into Middle Creek and along county roads 440 and 442.

Widespread flooding occurred on several rural roads in the area, including Collins Road, Town Road 730, Snyder Lane and Goody Hollow Road. Spaulding Hill Road was reported as impassable due to flood debris.
Barricades were requested to put out on Joe Sevario Road due to significant street  flooding.
Cars were reported stranded in flood waters in Jersey City.
Driver of car that stalled out in deep flood water had to be rescued on La Rochelle road east of highway 929. Significant street flooding occurred on many nearby streets.
Roberts and Pierce Creek Roads were flooded and covered with debris. Roads were impassable.
All lanes were closed due to flooding on the US 1&9 truck route northbound at the New Jersey Turnpike in Newark.

A Tonto National Forest service member shared photos from a forest service road near Pinal Peak showing evidence of a flash flood with debris across the road, including boulders/rocks and tree branches strewn across the road. In coordination with the WFO Phoenix Senior Service Hydrologist, it would have taken at least 6 inches of flowing water to move the debris in the photos. There were no reports of damage or injuries.
Multiple creeks were over their banks in the Town of Binghamton. Several roads were flooded, washed out and impassible.
NY 303 was closed due to flooding between Spruce Street and Orangeburg Road in Orangeburg.
A maximum 5 inch rain gauge had overtopped. Additional rain had fallen past that point in time.
Unofficial observation at residence. Nearby stations to the west reported between 5.3 and 5.7 inches of total rainfall. Most of the rain fell in the last 2 1/2 hours.
Hail ripped paint off of the observer's home and destroyed their garden plants.
ASOS station KNEW New Orleans Lakefront Airport measured gust of 44 mph or 38 knots from passing thunderstorm winds.

One to three inches of rain in 90 minutes in the Cornfield Canyon watershed caused flash flooding. As two females, who had exited their vehicle, were viewing the stream at Ocatillo Road, an additional rise in water levels swept them downstream. One was rescued about three quarters of a mile away while the other was finally located in the San Pedro River the next morning. Both sustained minor injuries.
A thunderstorm moved across Midland and produced wind damage. There were tree limbs blown down of four to five inches in diameter. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm produced wind damage in and near Midland. There were multiple trees with large branches broken or broken at the base. The time was estimated from radar. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding across Midland County. There were several roads under water across western Midland County, including Farm to Market Road 1788. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Emergency managers reported fallen trees close to Road PR-100 and PR-102 related to strong thunderstorm produced by the rainbands. The Cabo Rojo Raws station measured wind gusts up to 30 mph.
The Navarro County OEM reported street flooding and flooding in low-lying areas in and around the Corsicana. Minor street flooding was also reported in Mildred, Angus, and Mustang.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Colorado City. There were multiple low water crossing rescues that occurred around Colorado City. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Fallen tree caused downed power lines in Sector Barriada Borinquen.
Downed tree damaged a car in Sector Laberinto in Barrio Guatemala.
Pictures on social media showed standing water on residential yards and driveways.

A man was struck by lightning while fishing on the beach at Spessard Holland South Beach Park in Melbourne Beach. The man was taken to a local hospital with injuries. The associated isolated thunderstorm moved from the mainland across the barrier island to the Atlantic while producing occasional cloud to ground lightning strikes.
The ASOS at the Treasure Coast International Airport in Ft. Pierce, KFPR, measured a peak wind gust of 34 knots from the west as a thunderstorm crossed the airfield.
Media reports high water on street in the French Quarter at Rampart Street.
NWS employee reports multiple flooded streets with one with its sidewalk covered. Measured 4 inches of rain.
Video on social media shows flooded street in lower ninth ward. Water has gotten up to  almost the bumper of a car.
NWS employee reports multiple flooded streets at intersections and Broad Street is down to one lane in New Orleans near Mid City.
Station (SCHNV) 12.1 SE Ely (Ndot), Elevation 6687 feet.
More than one inch of rain in less than 1 hour in upper reaches of Huachuca Canyon flooded the canyon and flowed across Burt Rd at Fort Huachuca.
Two inches of rain in less than 1 hour caused extensive flooding of Arivaca Road between mile markers 10 and 16 with additional flash flooding farther north near Keystone Peak.
In Brockton, a house was struck by lightning on Pine Grove Drive, resulting in a fire.

Heavy rain near Capitan in Lincoln County resulted in the rapid rise of the Magado Creek near the Capitan Fairgrounds. The Magado Creek rose an estimated ten feet which caused the flooding of a low water crossing in the area and temporarily trapping two unoccupied vehicles. No injuries or fatalities were reported. Damages are estimated for the damage to the two vehicles.
More than 3 inches of rain in 90 minutes in Rio Rico Southwest caused flash flooding more than 1 foot deep across several roadways.
Report and photo posted via social media.
Several roads along Interstate 10 including the service roads were flooded after several inches of rain. Main Street near Walmart was also flooded.

Several debris flows occurred as a result of heavy rain over the eastern portion of the Grizzly Creek Fire burn scar. The debris covered both sides of Interstate 70 and ran all the way down to the Colorado River. Hourly rain rates exceeded 0.50 inches/hour. I-70 was closed in both directions for several hours due to cleanup operations.
Report of scattered road barriers/road closings throughout the city of Kenner from flash flooding.
Heavy rainfall of 1.44 inches.
A landspout touched down briefly in an open field.  No damage was observed.
Spotter noted that nearby crops were damaged and associated wind gusts from thunderstorm knocked down two power line poles.
Half inch sized hail also fell with the storm.
A landspout touched down briefly in an open field.  No damage was observed.

Thunderstorms produced heavy rain and flooding from Dewey and the Agua Fria River to Humbug Creek and Mayer. Water was flowing over roads in Dewey and Meyer. A river gauge in Meyer showed a two foot rise.
Severe winds to seventy mph damaged some corn crops.
A brief landspout tornado developed about 3 miles northeast of Clinton in an open mixed grass prairie. No damage was observed or reported.
The hail caused some crop damage.
A storm produced hail for nearly 30 minutes with large hail to quarter size occurring at the end of the storm.
Peak wind measured at an NDAWN station at 3 meters.
A storm produced hail for nearly 30 minutes with large hail to quarter size occurring at the end of the storm.
Peak wind measured at an NDAWN station at 10 meters.
The Globe RAWS weather station (QGLA3), south of Globe proper, measured a 59 mph thunderstorm wind gust. Timing was estimated from radar.
Large trees blown down. Report and photos posted via social media.
